summary: Configured node1 (VyOS) as a router between lan-a (node2, eth1/10.50.50.0/24) and lan-b (node3, eth2/10.60.60.0/24). Assigned node1's eth1=10.50.50.254 and eth2=10.60.60.254, saved config. Assigned persistent static IPs to node2's ens7 (10.50.50.11) and node3's ens7 (10.60.60.12) via /etc/network/interfaces.d/60-lan.cfg, each with a persistent route to the peer subnet via node1. ip_forward was already 1 on node1 and no firewall filters exist, so forwarding is unrestricted with no NAT (source addresses preserved). Verified bidirectional ping and TCP connectivity (via nc) with tcpdump confirming original source IPs (10.50.50.11 / 10.60.60.12) reach the peer unmodified. Then performed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol on all three nodes: captured boot_id baselines, restarted each node via native reboot, confirmed boot_id changed post-restart, and re-verified interface config, routes, and end-to-end connectivity (including source-IP-preserving TCP flow) after all three restarts completed.
actions_performed: Inspected node1/node2/node3 interfaces and routing to discover topology (node1 has eth0=uplink, eth1=lan-a, eth2=lan-b; node2/node3 have ens2=uplink, ens7=lan interface)
Determined eth1<->node2 and eth2<->node3 mapping via temporary IP assignment and ping tests
Configured VyOS node1: set interfaces ethernet eth1 address 10.50.50.254/24, eth2 address 10.60.60.254/24, committed and saved
Verified net.ipv4.ip_forward=1 and no firewall filters configured on node1 (default-allow forwarding)

Persisted static IP 10.50.50.11/24 on node2 ens7 and 10.60.60.12/24 on node3 ens7 via /etc/network/interfaces.d/60-lan.cfg, each including an 'up ip route replace' stanza for the peer subnet via node1
Applied routes live with ip route replace on node2 and node3
Verified ping node2<->node3 (ttl=63, one hop) and TCP flow via nc with tcpdump proving source IP preserved (10.50.50.11 seen directly on node3, no NAT)
Captured boot_id baseline on all 3 nodes
Restarted node1 via /sbin/reboot, polled until exec available, confirmed boot_id changed, verified eth1/eth2 config and ip_forward persisted, verified node2<->node3 ping recovered
Restarted node2 via sudo /sbin/reboot, confirmed boot_id changed, verified ens7 IP/route persisted and ping to node3 recovered

Restarted node3 via sudo /sbin/reboot, confirmed boot_id changed, verified ens7 IP/route persisted, ping to node2 recovered, and re-verified TCP flow with tcpdump showing preserved source IP post-restart

evidence.summary: Discovered node1 eth1/eth2 uplinks, confirmed via test-IP ping that eth1 maps to node2's lan-a link and eth2 maps to node3's lan-b link
